question.worked_solution:
We differentiate each component separately.

- For the $x$-component $x(t)=12\operatorname{ln}⁡(t),$ we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=\frac{12}{t},
$$

and therefore,

$$
{x}^{′}(2)=\frac{12}{2}=6.
$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t)=\frac{5}{2}{t}^{2},$ we have

$$
{y}^{′}(t)=5t,
$$

and therefore,

$$
{y}^{′}(2)=5(2)=10.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(2) & =⟨{x}^{′}(2),\,{y}^{′}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,10⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|{r}^{′}(2)| & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{10}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+100} \\  & =\sqrt{136} \\  & =2\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}
$$
